Members of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) hold a picket protest at the south gate of the House of Representatives in Quezon City on Monday, December 29, 2025, as Congress moves toward the ratification of the proposed 2026 national budget.
 
The group opposes the measure, saying it contains pork barrel allocations, unprogrammed appropriations, confidential funds, and large infrastructure spending, which it claims were inserted through alleged coordination between Congress and Malacañang. | via Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News

data.text:
Members of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan hold a protest action in front of the gate of the House of Representatives in Quezon City on Monday, Dec. 29, as lawmakers move to ratify the 2026 national budget. 

Protesters said the 2026 national budget continues to include allocations for lawmakers, unprogrammed appropriations, confidential funds, and massive infrastructure spending, which they oppose in light of corruption scandals involving government agencies and officials, including alleged irregularities in flood control projects. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB

IN PHOTOS │Members of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) hold a picket protest at the south gate of the House of Representatives on Monday, December 29, as Congress moves to ratify the 2026 national budget. The group calls for the rejection of what it describes as a pork barrel–laden spending plan, alleging collusion between Congress and Malacañang to insert lawmakers’ allocations, unprogrammed appropriations, confidential funds, and large infrastructure projects. Bayan warns that approval of the proposed budget could spark broader protests in 2026.

📸: Edd Castro
